Bertie County, Spring 2026

Payments

Bertie County is set to receive approximately $1.68M in opioid settlement funds from 2022 through 2038. They have received $501K to date with $1.18M more anticipated.

Spending Plans

Bertie County has not shared any spending plans.

NULL

Local governments must approve and share spending plans before spending opioid settlement funds. Local governments may not spend more than the approved amounts (although they may spend less). Exhibit A strategies are high-impact strategies for addressing the opioid overdose epidemic; Exhibit B strategies are from the national settlement agreements and are available to local governments after participating in a Collaborative Strategic Planning process.

Collaborative Strategic Planning Reports and Recommendations

Local govenments that wish to spend opioid settlement funds on any Exhibit B strategies must first engage in the Collaborative Strategic Planning process, resulting in a report and recommendations document submitted to the local governing board. This process is not required before authorizing spending on Exhibit A strategies.

Bertie County has not submitted any report and recommendations documents.

Past Spending

As of Summer 2025, Bertie County has not reported spending any settlement funds.

As a state, North Carolina has spent a total of $70.7M ; the top three most-funded strategies are Recovery Support Services ( 56 gov’ts, $19.6M ), Evidence-Based Addiction Treatment ( 39 gov’ts, $8.64M ), and Post-Overdose Response Team ( 36 gov’ts, $8.08M ).

Implementation Scale

Local governments are at varying stages of implementing opioid settlement strategies. For each funded strategy, local governments were asked to selec their State of Implementation from a list of 5 options:

  • Exploration and Planning
  • Preparation
  • Initial Implementation
  • Full Implementation
  • Further Expansion
